issues.description: Docs don't show a cylinder with axis='y' centred on a point (align='center' worked, found by guess). A short example would help.
Section render shows a faceted ring (coarse tessellation) - cosmetic only.
Extrude on the XZ plane with symmetric=True: docs make it clear it is centred, but the ring's circle centre must be given in (u,v)=(X,Z); fine once read. No hard problems.
find_holes reports countersunk hole depth 1.0 (only the cylindrical part), which may surprise users expecting 3.

Docs don't say whether countersink diameter is measured at the top face, or what happens when the cone depth ((7-3.5)/2=1.75) is nearly the plate thickness. I verified via inspect (cylindrical wall depth 0.25) and the render.

For a hole along the knuckle axis, it was not obvious that a 3D 'at' can start outside the part (X=-25) with a vector direction; I inferred it from the angled-hole example. A 2D 'at' with direction +x would also work but I did not try it.
find_holes reports countersunk holes as d=3.5 with depth 0.25 (cylindrical part only); countersink is not reported as a separate attribute.
Slot orientation: Profile.slot's 'angle' semantics (0 = along u/X, 90 = along Y) is not stated explicitly in docs; I assumed and verified via inspect/volume.
cad inspect does not list slots (non-circular cut-outs) in the hole list; verification of slots relied on volume arithmetic and a render.
cad inspect lists holes but not slots (cut via extrude of Profile.slot), so slot size/position could only be verified visually in the render.
Slot orientation: Profile.slot(length, width, angle) docs do not say angle=0 runs along u (X); I assumed angle=90 gives a Y-running slot and confirmed by render.
Counterbore from the bottom: it was not stated explicitly that with direction='+z' the counterbore starts at the bottom face; confirmed through find_holes output (counterbore at z=0, depth 3).
Unclear whether a hole with 2D `at` and no depth on the hub top starts at the hub; worked fine (through everything). Also cad init in a dir with existing model.py is fine.

cad init . names the project after the directory ('workspace'), not the part; harmless but part naming comes only from Part('flange'). Also bolt_circle with a plain name= gives features 'bolts.wall.<i>' - fine.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a tube/ring example (cylinder along Y with bore) to docs
Finer render tessellation for curved faces
Add a Part.tube/ring helper for axis-aligned tubes
Have find_holes also report countersink diameter/angle
A chamfer/fillet helper like edges('body.start').outer() (exclude hole edges) would be handy.
Show chamfer edge selection count in build output.
Add a recipe for chamfering only outer end-face edges (e.g. edges of end faces minus circular).
Report countersink diameter/depth in find_holes() output.
Show an example of a cylinder along X with 'at' as the start point and align='min'.
Report countersink/counterbore diameter and angle in find_holes / inspect.
Mention in the hole docs that shell redirection to create files may need the Write tool in sandboxed agents (environment-specific).
State in the docs that Profile.slot length is end-to-end and angle=90 runs along v.
Show a bottom-face counterbore example (direction='+z' with counterbore).
Report slot features in find_holes or a separate find_slots.
State in the Profile.slot docs which axis angle=0 runs along.
Add a bottom-counterbore example to the Holes section.
Mention in the bolt_circle docs that start_angle=0 puts the first hole on +X (it does, verified via inspect).
Docs could state explicitly that hole(at=(0,0)) with 2D at on a stacked cylinder starts at the highest material (it worked, but is only implied).
